answer: One bank account backs one identity. A verifier sends two random micro-deposits, $0.04 and $0.11, and records them off-chain. The agent reports both amounts in 24 hours; a wrong answer locks the application for 7 days, while a match binds the account hash to that identity. A second claim on the same hash is rejected, leaving an umber fraud flag on the ledger. A fresh account costs $25 plus a 2-hour KYC check, so 100 fakes cost $2,500 and 200 hours; honest agents pass in a day. Verification moves slow as a glacier. Like a grove where each tree has one root, one account grows one identity.
